title: 禅 · meditation; Chan; to abdicate
desc: One altar character, two civilizations: read shàn it yields thrones and sacrifices to earth; read chán it transliterates Sanskrit dhyāna and founds Zen.

title: 星 · star; celestial body; spark
desc: Born of the sun radical and a sprout, 星 names the stars, the planets, the week, movie fame, and the spark that starts prairie fires.

title: 电脑与网络 · Computers & the Internet
desc: The computer is an electric brain, downloading is "carrying down," and the number 666 is a compliment.

title: 度量衡 · Weights & Measures
desc: Fruit is priced by the half-kilo 斤, distance walks in 里, and an idiom about six of one and half a dozen still counts in base sixteen.

title: 看病 · Seeing a Doctor
desc: Getting sick in Chinese starts with a queue number, runs on the verb "look," and ends with the eternal prescription: drink more hot water.

title: 生意 · Doing Business
desc: Business in Chinese is literally "the meaning of life," merchants are named after a fallen dynasty, and the deal closes at the dinner table.

title: 数字系统 · The Chinese Number System
desc: Chinese numbers are built from eleven syllables and zero irregularity; the catch is that the system pivots on ten thousand, not one thousand.

title: 天气 · Talking About the Weather
desc: Rain falls, wind blows, and fog counts as a noun-verb drama: the small grammar of weather is a beginner's best conversation opener.

title: 结果补语 · resultative complements
desc: Chinese verbs describe the attempt; a second syllable reports the outcome. Listening is 听, but understanding what you heard is 听懂.

title: 可能补语 · potential complements
desc: Slide 得 or 不 inside a verb-result pair and it states ability: 听懂 is understood, 听得懂 is can understand, 听不懂 is the learner's anthem.

title: 离合词 · separable verbs
desc: Words that unzip: 见面 is to meet, but meeting him is 跟他见面 and meeting once is 见一次面, because the "word" is secretly verb plus object.

title: 又 · 再 · again, twice over
desc: Chinese has two agains: 又 looks backward at a repetition that happened, 再 looks forward to one still to come. 再见 is the proof.

title: 正反问 · A-not-A questions
desc: Chinese asks yes-no questions by offering both answers: 去不去 is "going, not going?", and the pattern replaces 吗 with built-in neutrality.

title: 工程 · Engineering
desc: From the carpenter's square inside 工 to the high-speed rail map, the vocabulary of a civilization that has always thought in projects.

title: 化学 · Chemistry
desc: The Chinese periodic table is a naming machine: one character per element, with the radical telling you its state at room temperature.

title: 生物 · Biology & the Naming of Living Things
desc: The panda is a bear-cat, the giraffe a long-necked deer, and the word for gene may be the best translation in the language.

title: 数学 · Mathematics
desc: The vocabulary of Chinese mathematics, where calculus is "tiny accumulation" and geometry was named by a Ming official translating Euclid.

title: 天文 · Astronomy
desc: The five visible planets are named for the five phases, comets are brooms, and the space program borrows its names from mythology.

title: 物理 · Physics
desc: Physics in Chinese is "the pattern of things," a phrase lifted from a Song-dynasty program for investigating the world.

title: 多少 · how much, how many
desc: Chinese builds its "how much" by welding many to few, part of a system where opposites fuse into the scale between them.
